title: Repair the App Router root layout
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/layout.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode: export default function Layout({children}: {children: React.ReactNode}) { return <main>{children}</main>; }

codeReviewFiles.newCode: export default function Layout({children}: {children: React.ReactNode}) { return <main>{children}</main>; }

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Build with a real root page and verify one html/body pair.
Navigate between two sibling pages and verify shared client state persists.
Reload a nested URL directly and verify the same shell.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: The root layout owns html and body; a nested layout must not create a second document.
Build with a real root page and verify one html/body pair.
alternativeApproaches: A template remounts its children during navigation and resets their state/effects. Use it for deliberate per-navigation lifecycle behavior, not as a workaround for stale authorization. Put authorization near protected data reads.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

verification: Build with a real root page and verify one html/body pair.
Navigate between two sibling pages and verify shared client state persists.
Reload a nested URL directly and verify the same shell.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
